title: elsa-tree/4
description: The shape of a Tree file (tree.json) of the ELSA decision-tree frontend. This schema is the STRUCTURE half of the contract: types, required keys, closed sets and the grammars of ids, language tags, file names, colours and URLs. It deliberately carries no maximum on any text a reader sees and no list maximum, because those are measured on the COUNTED TEXT of docs/specs/tree-format.md 3.8 -- Markdown links replaced by their text, Unicode code points counted -- which a JSON Schema cannot compute; they are the content rules of tree-format.md section 7 (V-LENGTH, V-LINES, V-COUNT), applied by the loader after this schema passes. The four maxLength keywords this schema does carry -- 64 on an id and 128 on each of the three file names -- are the exception tree-format.md 5.7 states: those are machine-facing tokens whose grammar is already ASCII, so a code-point count is a byte count and needs nothing from section 3.8; the caps keep an id or a file name from becoming a path or a header a server has to carry, and no reader ever sees them. Rules that need to read another part of the file (every localised text holds exactly the declared languages; every reference names an existing Node; every explainer is marked in the description) are content rules for the same reason. See docs/specs/tree-format.md and docs/adrs/ADR-118-json-schema.md.

$schema.description: A pointer to this schema, so a generic tool can find the contract from the file alone. Written first. The Trees in this repository write the origin-relative path, which resolves against whatever origin serves the Tree (docs/specs/application.md 15.1); a third party that publishes the schema elsewhere writes its absolute URL. The loader does not fetch it. The pattern matches the origin-relative path exactly, or an absolute http(s) URL that has a host and whose PATH ends /schemas/elsa-tree-4.json; ? and # are excluded throughout, so a query or a fragment cannot be what carries the name (V-SCHEMA).

format.description: The version of the contract this Tree is written against. A loader that does not know the value rejects the Tree (V-FORMAT).

languages.description: The languages every localised text in the Tree provides. The first entry is the default language. Order is meaningful.

root.description: The Node the walk starts at. Must be a question Node or a Terminal (V-ROOT).

nodes.description: Every Node of the Tree, as an array in the author's order. The order is the Tree's reading order; the loader indexes by id, so no Link depends on it.

id.description: An id (tree-format.md 3.1): lowercase ASCII letters and digits with single hyphens between groups. The colon is excluded, which is rule V-CROSS by construction.

nodeReference.description: The id of a Node in the same Tree (tree-format.md 3.2).

languageTag.description: A lowercase BCP 47 language tag (tree-format.md 3.3): en, nl, de, pt-br.

localisedText.description: A mapping from language tag to a non-empty string. That it holds exactly the languages the manifest declares is rule V-L10N, which needs `languages` and is therefore a content rule.

metadata.description: The author's bag. `version` is required and is a string (V-META); every other key is the author's own, kept and not interpreted. This is where a note that would have been a YAML comment goes. A key made only of digits is refused: an integer-like key is an array index to a JavaScript object, which moves it in front of every other key, and the canonical byte form of tree-format.md 3.7 -- version first, then the author's own keys in the order they were written -- would not survive a read and a write. Prefix such a key: note-2024, not 2024.

url.description: An absolute http:// or https:// URL. Linked to, never fetched by the application. The rule is the pattern, not a `format` keyword: `format` is annotation-only by default and its assertion behaviour differs between validators, so a schema that leans on it is a schema that means different things in different tools.

imageFileName.description: A file in this Tree's images/ folder (tree-format.md 3.5). Lowercase, no path separator, no dot segment.

logoFileName.description: A logo or icon file in this Tree's theme/ folder (tree-format.md 3.6).

fontFileName.description: A font file in this Tree's theme/ folder: woff2 and nothing else (tree-format.md 3.6).

theme.description: The look this Tree carries (tree-format.md 4.3). At least one of the three parts, and each part that is present is complete (V-THEME).

fonts.description: Font families, at most two and at most one per role; both maxima are content rules (V-COUNT, V-THEME).

weight.description: The font-weight descriptor as a string: one number 1 to 1000, or two separated by a space for a variable font's range.

colours.description: Exactly the seven roles, each six lowercase hexadecimal digits (tree-format.md 4.3.3). The set is closed: no eighth key, no missing key.

node.description: One Node (tree-format.md section 5). Its kind follows from which of `answers` and `terminal` is present: a question Node has `answers`, a Terminal has `terminal`, an explanation Node has neither. There is no `kind` key.

answers.description: V-KIND: a question Node is not also a Terminal.

terminal.description: V-KIND and V-TERMINAL: a Terminal has no Answers and no Options.

image.description: One picture. The first Image of a Node is its main image (tree-format.md 5.2); there is no `main` key and no `order` key.

answers.description: The yes/no Links. Exactly these two keys; in JSON they are strings by construction, so the YAML 1.1 trap that turned them into booleans is gone.

option.description: One entry of the clickable list. An Option has no Images of its own: the picture on its button is its target's main image (tree-format.md 5.4).

explainer.description: A term of this Node's description that carries a short explanation (tree-format.md 5.9). Marked in the description as [text](#id).

terminal.description: The explicit end-of-walk marker. The set of outcomes is closed; a Tree that needs a fifth value needs a new format number.
